cards.title: Surah 38 Account of God's Two Hands Forming Clay Adam and Iblis's Boast
cards.note: In Surah 38:71–85, God asks Iblis why he refused to prostrate before 'what I created with My two hands,' and Iblis boasts that he was made from fire while Adam was made from clay, matching the Syriac Cave of Treasures and Vita Adae et Evae 14–15.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir state that God honored Adam by fashioning him from clay with His two hands and commanding the angels to perform a prostration of honor, which Iblis rejected through analogical pride comparing fire to clay.
discussion.reply: Distinctive to Surah 38 is God's rebuke concerning 'what I created with My two hands' alongside Iblis's fire-over-clay argument. Genesis 1–3 contains no angelic prostration to Adam, whereas the Syriac Cave of Treasures depicts God fashioning Adam with His holy hands and the fallen prince refusing to bow because he is fire and spirit while Adam is dust, alongside Vita Adae et Evae 14–15.

cards.quranEn: [71] (Remember) when your Lord said to the angels: ‘Surely I am going to create a human being from clay. [72] When I have fashioned him, and breathed some of My spirit into him, fall down before him in prostration.’ [73] So the angels prostrated themselves – all of them together [74] – except Iblīs. He became arrogant, and was one of the disbelievers. [75] He said, ‘Iblīs! What prevented you from prostrating yourself before what I created with My two hands? Have you become arrogant, or are you one of the exalted?’ [76] He said, ‘I am better than him. You created me from fire, but You created him from clay.’ [77] He said, ‘Get out of here! Surely you are accursed! [78] surely My curse (is going to remain) on you until the Day of Judgment.’ [79] He said, ‘My Lord, spare me until the Day when they are raised up.’ [80] He said, ‘Surely you are one of the spared [81] – until the Day of the known time.’ [82] He said, ‘Then, by Your honor, I shall indeed make them err – all (of them) [83] – except for Your devoted servants among them.’ [84] He said, ‘(This is) the truth, and the truth I say: [85] I shall indeed fill Gehenna with you and those of them who follow you – all (of you)!’

cards.title: Mary Styled 'Daughter of 'Imran' (Amram of Numbers 26:59)
cards.note: Surah 66:12 directly calls Mary, the mother of Jesus, 'Mary, daughter of 'Imran' (Maryama bnata 'Imrana), assigning to her the patronymic of Miriam, daughter of Amram and sister of Aaron and Moses in Numbers 26:59.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir explain that 66:12 names Mary 'daughter of 'Imran' either after her biological father from the Davidic or priestly line, or by ancestral lineage to the Mosaic 'Imran (Amram), while Gabriel breathed into the sleeve of her garment.
discussion.reply: Whereas 19:28 addresses Mary as 'sister of Aaron' and 3:35 speaks of the 'wife of 'Imran,' 66:12 explicitly names Mary 'daughter of 'Imran' (Maryama bnata 'Imrana). In the Hebrew Bible and Septuagint (Numbers 26:59; Exodus 6:20), Amram ('Imran) is the Levitical father of Aaron, Moses, and their sister Miriam (Greek Mariam), thirteen centuries before Jesus' mother Mary (whose father in early Christian tradition is Joachim).

cards.title: Rival Claims Over Whether the Sleepers of the Cave Were Seven or Eight
cards.note: Surah 18:22 catalogues rival claims over the headcount of the youths in the cave (three, five, or seven with their dog as the eighth), mirroring the split between eight youths in Jacob of Serugh's Syriac homily and seven youths with a dog in Theodosius.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir report from Ibn 'Abbas that Christian denominations of Najran and Syria disputed whether the sleepers numbered three, five, or seven alongside their dog Qitmir, and that 18:22 endorses the count of seven youths plus their dog.
discussion.reply: Late antique Christian sources preserve the exact numerical divergence cited in 18:22: West-Syrian bishop Jacob of Serugh (d. 521) consistently numbers the youths of Ephesus as eight companions in his Syriac memra, whereas the Greek and Latin tradition represents them as seven brothers, to whom the sixth-century pilgrim Theodosius (De situ terrae sanctae 26) adds the dog Viricanus at their feet.

Still others say, ‘(There were) seven, the eighth of them was their dog.’ Say: ‘My Lord knows about their number. No one knows (about) them except a few.’ So do not dispute about them, except (on) an obvious point, and do not ask for a pronouncement about them from any of them.

sources.en: When the emperor Decius visits the city of Ephesus, he builds temples to several pagan deities and demands that the citizens offer sacrifices there; a group of eight Christian young men refuse to comply and are threatened with court action. When Decius leaves Ephesus for a while, the youths hide in a cave on the mountain in the city's vicinity, where God 'took their spirits and raised them up above, to heaven, and left a watcher to be guarding their limbs.' When Decius returns to the city, he orders the youths to be immured in the cave.

cards.title: Abraham Glancing at the Stars, Mocking Food Offerings, and the Furnace
cards.note: Surah 37:83–98 links three episodes: Abraham glancing at the stars and excusing himself as sick, mocking the food set before the silent idols before striking them, and being cast into a blazing furnace, combining Jubilees 12 and Bereishit Rabbah 38:13.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir explain that Abraham looked at the stars to feign illness so his people would leave him alone in the idol temple during their festival, allowing him to mock their food offerings and smash the statues with his right hand.
discussion.reply: Distinctive to Surah 37 is the astrological glance at the stars (37:88) paired with mocking the food offered to the idols (37:91). These motifs combine the second-century BC Book of Jubilees 12:16–18 (where Abram observes the stars at night before rejecting astrology) with Bereishit Rabbah 38:13 (where a woman brings a dish of fine flour as an offering before Abraham smashes the idols and faces Nimrod's fire).

[87] What do you think about the Lord of the worlds?’ [88] And he took a look at the stars, [89] and said, ‘Surely I am sick.’ [90] So they turned away from him, withdrawing. sources.en: One time, a certain woman came, carrying a dish of fine flour in her hand. She said to him: ‘Here, offer it before them.’ He arose, took a club in his hand, shattered all the idols, and placed the club in the hand of the largest among them. When his father came, he said to him: ‘Who did this to them?’ He said to him: ‘I will not lie to you, a certain woman came, carrying a dish of fine flour in her hand. cards.title: Iblis Refusing to Bow to Adam Formed from Dry Clay and Dark Mud
cards.note: Surah 15:26–42 contrasts creating man from sounding dry clay of dark molded mud (salsalin min hama'in masnun) with creating the jinn from scorching fire before Iblis refuses to bow to Adam, matching the Cave of Treasures and Vita Adae et Evae 14–16.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir interpret salsalin min hama'in masnun in 15:26–33 as dried clay formed from dark, altered mud that makes a ringing sound when struck, contrasting Adam's earthen origin with the smokeless scorching flame of the jinn.
discussion.reply: Surah 15 is the sole Quranic passage to use the formula 'dry clay from dark molded mud' (salsalin min hama'in masnun) and 'fire of scorching wind' (nar al-samum). The narrative structure — God breathing His spirit into clay-formed Adam, the angels bowing, Iblis refusing to worship a creature of dust, and his banishment until the appointed time — parallels the Syriac Cave of Treasures and Vita Adae et Evae 14–16.

cards.quranEn: [26] Certainly We created the human from dry clay, from molded mud, [27] and the (ancestor of the) jinn, We created him before (that) from scorching fire. [28] (Remember) when your Lord said to the angels: ‘Surely I am going to create a human being from dry clay, from molded mud. [29] When I have fashioned him, and breathed some of My spirit into him, fall down before him in prostration.’ [30] So the angels prostrated themselves – all of them together [31] – except Iblīs. He refused to be with the ones who prostrated themselves. [32] He said, ‘Iblīs! What is (the matter) with you that you are not with the ones who prostrated themselves?’ [33] He said, ‘I am not (one) to prostrate myself before a human being whom you have created from dry clay, from molded mud.’ [34] He said, ‘Get out of here! Surely you are accursed! [35] Surely the curse (is going to remain) on you until the Day of Judgment.’ [36] He said, ‘My Lord, spare me until the Day when they are raised up.’ [37] He said, ‘Surely you are one of the spared [38] – until the Day of the known time.’ [39] He said, ‘My Lord, because You have made me err, I shall indeed make (things) appear enticing to them on the earth, and I shall indeed make them err – all (of them) [40] – except for Your devoted servants among them.’ [41] He said, ‘This is the straight path (incumbent) on Me. [42] Surely My servants – you will not have any authority over them, except for whoever follows you of the ones who are in error.

cards.title: Qarun, Pharaoh, and Haman Grouped as Arrogant Opponents of Moses
cards.note: Surah 29:39–40 groups Qarun (Korah), Pharaoh, and Haman together as recipients of Moses' clear signs who acted arrogantly on earth before being destroyed by earth-swallowing and drowning, combining Numbers 16:1–3 and Esther 3:1.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir explain that in 29:39–40 Moses brought clear signs to Pharaoh, his vizier Haman, and the wealthy Israelite Qarun in Egypt, after which God caused the earth to swallow Qarun (28:81) and drowned Pharaoh, Haman, and their hosts in the sea.
discussion.reply: In the Hebrew Bible, Korah (Qarun) is an Israelite Levite who rebels against Moses in the Sinai wilderness after the Exodus (Numbers 16:1–3), whereas Haman the Agagite is a fifth-century BC Persian courtier under King Artaxerxes in Susa (Esther 3:1). Talmud Bavli Sanhedrin 110a connects Korah's wealth to Joseph's buried treasures in Egypt, explaining how Korah came to be linked with Pharaoh's court.

cards.quranEn: [39] And Qārūn, and Pharaoh, and Haman – certainly Moses brought them the clear signs, but they became arrogant on the earth. Yet they did not outrun (Us). [40] We seized each one for his sin. We sent a sandstorm against one of them, and another of them was seized by the cry, and We caused the earth to swallow (yet) another of them, and We drowned (still) another of them. Yet God was not one to do them evil, but they did themselves evil.

cards.title: Surah 2 Account of the Angels Bowing to Adam After the Naming Scene
cards.note: Immediately after Adam recites the names of all things before the angels in 2:31–33, Surah 2:34 narrates God commanding the angels to prostrate before Adam while Iblis refuses in arrogance, matching Vita Adae et Evae 13–15 and the Cave of Treasures.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir explain that in 2:34 God commanded the angels to bow to Adam as a greeting of honor after Adam demonstrated superior knowledge by naming the creatures, whereas Iblis refused out of envy and pride.
discussion.reply: Unlike 7:12, 15:33, and 38:76, which give Iblis's fire-versus-clay argument, 2:34 places the command to prostrate immediately after Adam's naming of the creatures (2:31–33) and attributes Iblis's refusal simply to arrogance (istakbara). This sequence directly parallels the Syriac Cave of Treasures, where Adam names all creatures on his throne before the angels bow the knee and the rebellious archangel refuses.

cards.title: The Companions of the Cave and al-Raqim Sealed in Sleep for Years
cards.note: Surah 18:9–12 introduces the youths of the Cave and al-Raqim (the inscription) whose ears are sealed in sleep for generations before awakening, matching Gregory of Tours' account of the lead tablets placed at the sealed entrance of the Ephesian cave.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record multiple early explanations of al-Raqim in 18:9, with Ibn 'Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and Wahb ibn Munabbih identifying it as an inscribed tablet of stone or lead recording the names and story of the youths at the cave entrance.
discussion.reply: Distinctive to 18:9–12 is the pairing of 'the Companions of the Cave and al-Raqim' (ashaba l-kahfi wa-l-raqim) with the sealing of their ears in sleep. In the sixth-century Passio Septem Dormientium of Gregory of Tours (translated from Syriac), two Christians named Theodore and Ruben write the history of the youths on lead tablets and place them inside the blocked mouth of the cave.

[10] (Remember) when the young men took refuge in the cave, and said, ‘Our Lord, grant us mercy from Yourself, and furnish the right (course) for us in our situation.’ [11] So We sealed up their ears in the cave for a number of years, [12] and then We raised them up (again), so that We might know which of the two factions would better count (the length of) time (they had) remained (there).

cards.title: Believing Youths Standing Before the Pagan Ruler and Fleeing to the Cave
cards.note: Surah 18:13–16 narrates how the believing youths stood up to proclaim that their Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, rejected their people's idols, and withdrew into the cave, matching Gregory of Tours' account of the youths defying Decius.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir recount that the youths were noble sons of Ephesus who stood before the idolatrous king Daqyanus (Decius), refused to offer pagan sacrifices, and fled to a mountain cave outside the city to preserve their faith.
discussion.reply: Whereas 18:9–12 summarizes the sleep in the cave and 18:17–20 describes their awakening and silver coin, 18:13–16 focuses on their public confession before the pagan court (idh qamu fa-qalu Rabbuna Rabbu l-samawati wa-l-ard). Gregory of Tours' sixth-century Latin Passio (translated from a fifth-century Syriac original) opens with the noble youths arrested before Emperor Decius, refusing pagan sacrifice, and retreating to the cave.

cards.quranEn: [13] We shall recount to you their story in truth: Surely they were young men who believed in their Lord, and We increased them in guidance. [14] We strengthened their hearts, when they stood up and said, ‘Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth. We do not call on any god other than Him. Certainly we would then have spoken an outrageous thing. [15] These people of ours have taken gods other than Him. If only they would bring some clear authority concerning them! Who is more evil than the one who forges a lie against God? [16] When you have withdrawn from them and what they serve instead of God, take refuge in the cave. Your Lord will display some of His mercy to you, and will furnish some relief for you in your situation.’

(3) They were granted some time to think and change their minds, while the emperor visited another city; they sold their possessions and gave the proceeds to the poor, and withdrew to a cave on Mount Celion, selecting Malchus to go in secret to the city to purchase supplies. cards.title: The Resurrection Proof and Building a Sanctuary Over the Sleepers' Cave
cards.note: Surah 18:21 states that the sleepers were discovered to confirm the resurrection of the dead, after which the authorities resolved to build a sanctuary (masjidan) over their cave, matching Gregory of Tours' Passio on Emperor Theodosius II.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir explain that God caused the citizens to discover the youths so the king and his divided subjects would know that bodily resurrection is true, after which the prevailing party built a sanctuary over the cave entrance.
discussion.reply: Surah 18:21 preserves two specific narrative elements from the Christian legend of Ephesus: first, that the awakening took place specifically to settle a theological controversy over the bodily resurrection under Emperor Theodosius II; and second, that after the youths fell asleep again, the authorities proposed building a shrine or basilica (basilica magna) directly over their bodies at the cave.

cards.quranEn: So We caused (the people of the city) to stumble upon them, in order that they might know that the promise of God is true, and that the Hour – (there is) no doubt about it. When they argued among themselves about their situation, they said, ‘Build over them a building. Their Lord knows about them.’ Those who prevailed over their situation said, ‘We shall indeed take (to building) a place of worship over them.’

cards.title: Solomon Taught the Speech of Birds and Hearing the Ant in the Valley
cards.note: Surah 27:15–19 states that Solomon was taught the speech of birds (mantiq al-tayr), marshaled ranks of jinn, men, and birds, and understood an ant warning its colony, matching Solomon's rule over birds and demons in Targum Sheni on Esther 1:2.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir explain that God granted Solomon miraculous comprehension of animal and avian languages alongside command over jinn and human armies, enabling him to hear the queen ant warning her colony as his forces marched past.
discussion.reply: In 1 Kings 4:33, Solomon composes proverbs concerning trees, beasts, birds, and creeping things. Late antique Jewish exegesis in Targum Sheni on Esther 1:2 and Talmud Bavli Gittin 68a transforms this botanical and zoological wisdom into literal sovereignty over wild beasts, birds of the sky, and demons (shedim), explicitly stating that Solomon knew the speech of all of them and they understood his speech.

cards.title: Surah 26 Dialogue of Abraham Asking Whether Terah's Idols Hear or Help
cards.note: In Surah 26:69–89, Abraham asks his father and people whether their idols hear them when they call or can benefit or harm them, and urges worship of the Creator who provides food and drink, reproducing Book of Jubilees 12:2–5.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir view Abraham's catechism in 26:70–74 as a prophetic demonstration showing the helplessness of carved statues and the insufficiency of blind ancestral imitation (wajadna aba'ana kadhalika yaf'alun).
discussion.reply: Unlike 21:51–70 and 37:83–98, Surah 26:69–89 omits the smashing of the idols and the fiery furnace, focusing on Abraham's verbal interrogation of his father over whether the idols hear prayers or bring profit (hal yasma'unakum idh tad'un aw yanfa'unakum). That exact question appears in the second-century BC Book of Jubilees 12:2–5 ('What help and profit have we from those idols... For there is no spirit in them').

cards.title: Pharaoh Slaughtering Israelite Sons Beside Haman and Their Hosts in Egypt
cards.note: Surah 28:3–6 recounts Pharaoh slaughtering Israelite sons while sparing their women, and pairs Haman and his forces (Fir'awna wa-Hamana wa-junudahuma) directly with Pharaoh during the Exodus 1 infanticide, combining Exodus 1:16–22 and Esther 3:1–6.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir identify Haman in 28:6 as Pharaoh's chief minister and advisor in Egypt during the oppression of the Israelites, distinguishing him from the Persian Haman of the Book of Esther or treating the name as an Egyptian court title.
discussion.reply: In Exodus 1:16–22 and Talmud Bavli Sotah 12a, Pharaoh decrees that newborn Hebrew males be cast into the Nile without any minister named Haman. Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite appears a millennium later in Esther 3:1–6 as the grand vizier of the fifth-century BC Persian king Artaxerxes/Ahasuerus in Susa who plotted to exterminate the Jews of the Persian Empire.

cards.title: Moses Sent to Pharaoh, Haman, and Qarun and Defended by a Royal Believer
cards.note: Surah 40:23–29 sends Moses to Pharaoh, Haman, and Qarun (40:24) and introduces a believer from Pharaoh's house who warns the royal council that if Moses is truthful God's punishment will strike them (40:28), matching Sotah 11a and Acts 5:34–39.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir explain that Moses was sent to Pharaoh, his minister Haman, and the wealthy Israelite Qarun in Egypt, while a Coptic kinsman of Pharaoh who secretly believed spoke up in the royal assembly to dissuade Pharaoh from executing Moses.
discussion.reply: Surah 40:23–29 combines two distinct elements: first, 40:24 groups Egypt's Pharaoh with Haman (the Persian courtier of Esther 3:1) and Qarun/Korah (an Israelite Levite whose Egyptian treasure keys are described in Talmud Sanhedrin 110a); second, 40:28 puts on the lips of a royal advisor the conditional warning of Gamaliel before the Sanhedrin in Acts 5:38–39 alongside Pharaoh's advisors in Sotah 11a.

sources.ref: Talmud Bavli Sotah 11a (Pharaoh's Counsel Against Israel and the Three Royal Advisors)
sources.workSub: Talmud Bavli, Sotah 11a
sources.en: Three noteworthy people were consulted by Pharaoh in that counsel where Pharaoh questioned what should be done with the Jewish people. They were Balaam, and Job, and Yitro. Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba teaches what occurred to each of them: Balaam, who advised Pharaoh to kill all sons born to the Jewish people, was punished by being killed in the war with Midian (see Numbers 31:8). Job, who was silent and neither advised nor protested, was punished by suffering, as detailed in the eponymous book in the Bible. Yitro, who ran away as a sign of protest.

cards.title: Mary and Her Son Sheltered on High Ground with a Flowing Spring
cards.note: Surah 23:50 states that God gave the son of Mary and his mother refuge on high ground with a restful hollow and a flowing spring (rabwatin dhati qararin wa-ma'in), combining the mountain refuge of Protevangelium 22 with the spring of Pseudo-Matthew 20.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir report varying geographical identifications among early commentators for the 'high ground with a restful hollow and flowing spring' in 23:50, including Damascus, Ramla, Jerusalem, and Egypt during the flight from Herod.
discussion.reply: Unlike 19:23–26, where Mary gives birth alone beside a palm tree and a stream (sariyyan), 23:50 describes God sheltering both the son of Mary and his mother on high ground (rabwah) with a flowing spring. This combines the cleft mountain refuge of the Protevangelium of James 22 with the miraculous spring of water opened beneath the palm tree during the flight to Egypt in Pseudo-Matthew 20.

sources.en: And Elizabeth , having heard that they were searching for John, took him and went up into the hill-country, and kept looking where to conceal him. And there was no place of concealment. And Elizabeth , groaning with a loud voice, says: O mountain of God , receive mother and child. And immediately the mountain was cleft, and received her. And a light shone about them, for an angel of the Lord was with them, watching over them.

sources.en: Then Jesus said to it: Raise yourself, O palm tree, and be strong, and be the companion of my trees, which are in the paradise of my Father; and open from your roots a vein of water which has been hid in the earth, and let the waters flow, so that we may be satisfied from you. And it rose up immediately, and at its root there began to come forth a spring of water exceedingly clear and cool and sparkling. And when they saw the spring of water, they rejoiced with great joy , and were satisfied, themselves and all their cattle and their beasts. Wherefore they gave thanks to God .
